question: When is the om syllable with fourth ending a name rather than a seed?
premises: Om with fourth ending can be a name
In Ganapati and similar cases it becomes a seed
Not every such formula is declared a seed
inference: Name and seed are distinguished by context and deity sequence, not by om alone.
uncertainties: natiriti is obscure and may be mis-split
caturthyantā may describe the name or the mantra
plain_english: Then the om syllable ending in the fourth form is a name, thus bowing; in order, among Ganapati and others it would be a seed mantra, in which cases it is not declared so.
